problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions such that ${\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=18,{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{1}{2}g(x)\,\text{d}x=5,$ and ${\int }_{3}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x=4.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=8$ and ${\int }_{2}^{0}2f(x)\,\text{d}x=4.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{0}2f(x)\,\text{d}x & =4 \\ 2{\int }_{2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =4 \\ -2{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =4 \\ {\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(-2)+8 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
